issue.title: Prototype the Smart and Literal writing behavior

in_scope: Exact English Smart vs Literal before/after examples for Raja approval
Must-change and must-preserve counterexamples as full proposed strings
Open product decisions with complete mutually exclusive alternatives
Structured formatting_changes vs grammar_changes notes (human labels only)
out_of_scope: Release scoring, thresholds, denominators, and CI pass/fail gates (#103 after approval)
Machine safety validation, protected/forbidden matchers, lexical sequence evaluators (#100)
Structured edit/patch representation and rejection policy (#100)
Locked command parser/state-machine implementation contract (choose D_cmd first; implement in #103)
HTML/UI prototypes, live ASR, Groq calls, Delivery paths

decisions.title: Command syntax strategy
decisions.question: How should explicit formatting commands be recognized in the Validated Transcript? This is a product choice; #99 does not lock a parser.
decisions.recommendation: Prefer A (explicit introducer) for meaning safety; accept B only if Raja wants Wispr-like bare phrases and accepts noun-phrase ambiguity risk on counterexamples.

options.label: Explicit introducer
options.summary: Only `command <phrase>` fires. Bare lexicon phrases are ordinary speech. `literal command <phrase>` escapes to spoken words without firing.

options.label: Natural bare commands
options.summary: Bare phrases may fire as commands with an explicit literal escape for word-sense. Accepts documented ambiguity risk on noun phrases (bullet train, brand new line, etc.).

decisions.title: Terminal punctuation after paragraph command
decisions.question: When a new paragraph command fires, should Smart add terminal periods on short multi-word fragments?
decisions.recommendation: Yes for fragments with two or more content words.

options.label: Breaks only
options.summary: Emit paragraph break and case lines; no added periods.

options.label: Smart terminal punct
options.summary: Also add periods on multi-word fragments.

decisions.title: List inference without list commands
decisions.question: May Smart invent bullets/lists without spoken number/bullet commands?

options.label: Infer bullets
options.summary: Allow Smart to invent list structure.

decisions.title: Capitalization inside quotes
decisions.question: When quote commands fire, may Smart sentence-case a full quoted sentence?
decisions.recommendation: Preserve validated in-quote casing by default.

options.label: Sentence-case full quotes
options.summary: Also case inside full quoted sentences.

decisions.title: Double negatives
decisions.question: Should Minimal Grammar standardize double negatives, or preserve spoken voice?

decisions.title: Email greeting structure
decisions.question: Should Smart invent a greeting line and blank line for hi <name> openings?
decisions.recommendation: Only for clear hi/hello/dear openings; else single paragraph.

decisions.title: Oxford comma
decisions.question: Prefer Oxford comma in Smart serial lists?
